subject: New workstreams onboarding & API key provisioning — rollout proposal
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightharborhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New workstreams onboarding & API key provisioning — rollout proposal

Hi Elena,

Great speaking earlier — thanks for walking through the two new internal workstreams (Claims Assist and Member Insights). Per our conversation, the team expects each new app to start low-volume testing in September and scale to production traffic by mid-November. To keep things smooth on our side, I drafted a short rollout proposal and the key mapping we discussed.

High level proposal:
- Stage 1 (Pilot, Sept 6–20): 2 API keys (one per app), sandbox-only, rate limit 5 rps per key.
- Stage 2 (Ramp, Oct 4–Nov 12): 6 total keys (3 per app) for parallel environments (canary/staging/prod), burst quotas enabled, target 25k tokens/day aggregated.
- Stage 3 (Prod, from Nov 15): Autoscaling pool on Dedicated capacity (reserved), SLA target 99.95% P95 latency for shortest prompt path.

Attached: RBW-BrightHarbor-Addendum-v1.0.pdf (proposed addendum for term+capacity) and BH-apps-key-mapping.csv (per-app key map + initial quotas).

Next steps I propose:
1) Your procurement & legal to review the addendum (I can loop in our legal if you prefer).
2) You confirm the internal stakeholders who will manage keys and approve staging schedules.
3) Quick sync with Monica and Ben next week to confirm quota profiles and provisioning timing.

Can you confirm procurement contact and any specific security checklist items beyond SOC2 we should expect?

Cheers,
Diego
Account Manager — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RBW-BrightHarbor-Addendum-v1.0.pdf]
[Attachment: BH-apps-key-mapping.csv]
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightharborhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightharborhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: New workstreams onboarding & API key provisioning — rollout proposal

Diego — thanks for the proposal and the attachments. Quick responses:
- Procurement contact is Marco Alvarez (procurement@brightharborhealth.com) — copying him.
- Security: we will run your standard security questionnaire but also need the data residency clause (we prefer us-east) and explicit KMS integration details for keying.
- Capacity: the 25k tokens/day looks in-line as a starting forecast; Claims Assist may spike during batch runs (we estimate up to 120k tokens/day on peak days).

Marco, can you confirm the timeline for legal review? We’d like to avoid delaying the Sept pilot.

Elena
Director of Product — Bright Harbor Health
From: Marco Alvarez <procurement@brightharborhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightharborhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 12:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: New workstreams onboarding & API key provisioning — rollout proposal

Thanks both — procurement can turn on review this week. Couple of asks:
- Please provide a one-page summary of price impact for the increased committed capacity and what the billing change will look like (monthly vs. usage).
- For contract changes: does the addendum require a term extension or is this additive to the existing agreement?

I’ll have a preliminary note to legal by Friday.

—Marco
Senior Manager, Procurement — Bright Harbor Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightharborhealth.com>, Marco Alvarez <procurement@brightharborhealth.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New workstreams onboarding & API key provisioning — rollout proposal

Hi Elena / Marco — Monica from Customer Success here. Thanks for the details Marco — happy to put together the one-pager on pricing cadence. A few operational notes from the rollout perspective:

Provisioning & rollout specifics:
- API keys: we’ll create sandbox keys within 48 hours of approval and prod keys within 5 business days after the signed addendum. Keys will be labeled with project, environment, and owner.
- Quotas: we’ll set conservative rate limits for pilot, and the SE team (Ben) will run load tests during the ramp window.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (we’ll need a role ARN for the HB account).
- Data residency: we can pin inference to us-east region if requested — we’ll add that to the provisioning checklist.

I’ll assemble the operational checklist and the 1-page billing summary and share by EOD Friday.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot-run-checklist.docx]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@brightharborhealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: New workstreams onboarding & API key provisioning — rollout proposal

Elena / team — quick SE note on load and cost:
- If Claims Assist hits the 120k token/day peak, we recommend enabling KV-prefix caching for the batch pipeline and a partially quantized endpoint for lower-cost inference on non-critical responses. That approach typically reduces token compute cost by ~30% while maintaining answer quality.
- Pricing impact: the attached addendum has two options — incremental usage billing or a small committed buffer (we usually propose the committed buffer for predictability). Diego, I’ve highlighted the specific lines in RBW-BrightHarbor-Addendum-v1.0.pdf for Marco.

Happy to run a 30-min technical runbook session next Tue (Aug 10) with your engineers.

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced in earlier thread: RBW-BrightHarbor-Addendum-v1.0.pdf]
